evals.prompt: The settings page in this existing React app feels visually flat. Build three distinct layout and hierarchy directions in the project so I can compare them in the browser. Keep the experiments reversible.
evals.expected_output: Runnable in-project variants that expose meaningful layout and hierarchy tradeoffs and can be compared in the browser.
assertions: The work is implemented as runnable code in the existing project.
The variants differ in meaningful design decisions rather than superficial labels.
The comparison path is reversible and does not require production hardening.

evals.prompt: Explore two motion treatments for expanding cards in the current SwiftUI app. Exercise both in the target simulator and explain which interaction qualities each direction emphasizes.
evals.expected_output: Two working motion treatments in the SwiftUI project, verified in the target simulator with a concise comparison.
assertions: The motion directions are implemented in SwiftUI rather than represented as static mockups.
The important interaction is exercised in the target simulator.
The comparison connects implementation differences to interaction qualities.

evals.prompt: I want to compare a compact and an editorial navigation treatment across mobile and desktop in our existing web app. Make both directions easy to toggle and use the app's real content and tokens.
evals.expected_output: Two project-native responsive navigation variants using real content and design tokens with a practical comparison mechanism.
assertions: Both directions run inside the existing web application.
The variants use real content and existing design tokens where practical.
Mobile and desktop behavior are rendered or exercised before reporting the result.

evals.prompt: I'm redesigning the episode-status control in our SwiftUI app. I have a compact pill and a progress-ring idea, but I want your ideas too. Let's decide which directions are worth seeing before you build them with realistic watched, unwatched, and airing states.
evals.expected_output: A concise set of materially distinct directions followed, after selection, by a fixture-backed comparison in the repository's existing SwiftUI preview or native development surface.
assertions: The agent contributes distinct directions and waits for selection because the prompt explicitly asks to decide before building.
The selected variants use the same representative watched, unwatched, and airing fixtures so their design decisions are comparable.
The implementation reuses an existing SwiftUI preview, preview catalog, or native development surface rather than creating a detached web mockup.
The result identifies which experimental controls or variants would be removed when a direction is graduated.

evals.prompt: The reaction affordance in our React Native messenger still feels unresolved. Build the strongest three treatments so I can switch among them on-device with the same conversations and choose one. This repo already has Storybook and fixture providers.
evals.expected_output: Three meaningful reaction treatments in the existing on-device Storybook, driven by resettable shared conversation fixtures and exercised in the native simulator or development client.
assertions: The comparison reuses the repository's existing React Native Storybook and fixture providers.
The same conversation content and relevant interaction state are used across treatments.
The variants are exercised on the native platform rather than evaluated only as source code or static images.
Story and comparison-only code remain outside the production application boundary.

evals.prompt: Try a few treatments for the related-project cards in my Next.js portfolio and put them somewhere I can toggle while viewing the real page. There is no Storybook, and I need to compare the hover behavior plus compact and wide layouts before picking one.
evals.expected_output: Several meaningful card treatments behind a lightweight in-app development comparison control, using stable page content and verified across pointer and responsive states.
assertions: The agent uses a reversible project-local lab, development control, route, or variant picker because Storybook is absent.
The comparison holds page content and state constant while varying named design decisions.
Hover behavior and both compact and wide layouts are exercised in the browser.
The result explains how the temporary comparison surface will be removed or retained after selection.

evals.prompt: Before building, propose three directions for a new section header in this SwiftUI app: one that strictly follows the existing design system, one that stretches it, and one that deliberately diverges. Inspect the repository enough to ground the choices, keep the header's content and behavior comparable, and let me choose which versions to build.
evals.expected_output: Three repository-grounded directions at deliberate design-system distances, with stable foundations, named departures, and a selection gate before implementation.
assertions: The agent inspects repository evidence and distinguishes protected foundations from component conventions that may vary.
The faithful direction works within established tokens, primitives, interaction patterns, and visual language.
The stretch direction extends one named system pattern or rule, while the divergent direction names what it departs from and what remains protected.
All directions preserve comparable content, behavior, state, and accessibility constraints rather than differing only by color or decoration.
The agent stops for selection before implementation because the prompt asks to choose first.
